extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students in complex analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Study and construction of entire functions via Weierstrass products, the Hadamard factorization for finite-order entire functions, and analytic properties/factorizations of the Gamma function (with preparatory examples such as sine and cotangent product/sum formulas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product formula for sine
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from the cotangent sum formula; shown by comparing structural properties (periodicity, principal part at integers, singularities) and proving the quotient of two candidate functions is entire and bounded (Liouville) hence constant; constant determined by evaluating the limit at 0. Includes discussion of symmetric summation for divergent half-series and bounding arguments for large imaginary part to show boundedness of the difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cotangent sum formula
rubrics_metrics.description: π cot πz = Σ_{n=−∞}^∞ 1/(z + n) = 1/z + Σ_{n=1}^∞ (2z)/(z^2 − n^2) (the symmetric summation interpretation is required where the separate positive/negative halves do not converge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holds for all complex z not an integer; justification uses periodicity, local principal part near 0, and symmetry of summation (limit as N→∞ of sum over |n|≤N). Used as a key step to obtain product formula for sine by integrating structural properties and comparing meromorphic structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizing properties for π cot πz
rubrics_metrics.description: F(z)=π cot πz satisfies: (i) F(z+1)=F(z) (periodicity), (ii) F(z)=1/z + F0(z) with F0 analytic near 0, (iii) F has simple poles at integers and no other singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three properties are used to show equality with the symmetrically summed series and to reduce proofs to showing boundedness and Liouville-type conclusions for differences of functions with the same structural properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass product existence theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any sequence {a_n} of complex numbers with |a_n| → ∞, there exists an entire function f that vanishes at all z = a_n and nowhere else; any other such entire function is of the form f(z)e^{g(z)} with g entire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses canonical factors E_k(z) to correct naive products Π(1 − z/a_n) so as to force convergence without introducing new zeros. Multiplicities are accommodated via repetitions in the sequence. Uniqueness modulo an exponential factor follows because quotient of two such entire functions is entire and nowhere vanishing, hence an exponential of an entire function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical Weierstrass factors (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: E_0(z) = 1 − z; for k ≥ 1, E_k(z) = (1 − z) e^{z + z^2/2 + ... + z^k/k}. The integer k is called the degree of the canonical factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors are chosen so that E_k(z) has the same zero at z=1 as (1−z) but with exponential correction terms that guarantee better convergence properties of infinite products formed from them. Degree k is adjustable to control convergence depending on growth of zero sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local small-z bound for canonical factors (Lemma 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If |z| ≤ 1/2 then |1 − E_k(z)| ≤ c |z|^{k+1} for some c > 0 (indeed one can take c = 2e independent of k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses logarithm power series to express E_k(z) = e^w with w = −Σ_{n=k+1}^∞ z^n/n and bounds on |w|. This lemma underpins uniform estimates used to show convergence of products when |z/a_n| ≤ 1/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass product construction for prescribed zeros
rubrics_metrics.description: Given zero of order m at origin and nonzero zeros a_n, define f(z) = z^m Π_{n=1}^∞ E_{k_n}(z/a_n) with suitable choices of degrees k_n so product converges and produces zeros exactly at a_n with correct multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof splits factors into finitely many with |a_n| ≤ 2R and infinitely many with |a_n| > 2R; uses Lemma 4.2 to bound deviations and known product convergence propositions to show holomorphy and lack of extraneous zeros within any disc |z| < R, and since R arbitrary gives entire function. Choice of k_n must ensure Σ |a_n|^{−(k_n+1)} converges; one often chooses k_n to grow to meet this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of growth and zero-count relation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an entire function f has growth order ≤ ρ (|f(z)| ≤ A e^{B|z|^ρ}) then its zero-count n(r) satisfies n(r) ≤ C r^ρ for large r; conversely if s > ρ then Σ |a_n|^{-s} < ∞ for the nonzero zeros {a_n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relation links distribution of zeros to growth order and is a key quantitative input to Hadamard factorization (choice of common degree for canonical factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hadamard factorization theorem (Theorem 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is entire with growth order ρ_0 and k is integer with k ≤ ρ_0 < k+1, and a_n are the nonzero zeros of f, then f(z) = e^{P(z)} z^m Π_{n=1}^∞ E_k(z/a_n), where P is a polynomial of degree ≤ k and m is multiplicity at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This refines Weierstrass' theorem for finite-order functions: a single constant degree k suffices for all canonical factors and the remaining entire factor is an exponential of a polynomial. The proof uses lower bounds for canonical products away from small forbidden discs and growth estimates to deduce polynomiality of the log factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower bounds for canonical products away from zeros (Lemma 5.2 and 5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 5.2: |E_k(z)| ≥ e^{−c |z|^{k+1}} for |z| ≤ 1/2, and |E_k(z)| ≥ |1−z| e^{−c'|z|^k} for |z| ≥ 1/2. Lemma 5.3: For any s with ρ_0 < s < k+1, Π_{n=1}^∞ E_k(z/a_n) ≥ e^{−c |z|^s} except possibly when z lies in the union of discs centered at a_n of radius |a_n|^{−k−1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lemmas provide quantitative lower bounds on canonical products in the complement of small discs around zeros; split product into |a_n|>2|z| and |a_n|≤2|z| parts and use previous estimates plus convergence of Σ |a_n|^{-s}. The excluded small discs are radii |a_n|^{−k−1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of circles avoiding forbidden discs (Corollary 5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a sequence of radii r_m → ∞ such that on |z| = r_m the canonical product Π E_k(z/a_n) ≥ e^{−c |z|^s}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses covering argument: forbidden discs around |a_n| have total small measure so one can find radii in each large integer interval [L,L+1] avoiding them; then apply Lemma 5.3 on those circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomiality lemma for harmonic majorants (Lemma 5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If g is entire and u = Re(g) satisfies u(z) ≤ C r^s whenever |z|=r for a sequence r→∞, then g is a polynomial of degree ≤ s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Cauchy integral formula Fourier/coefficient extraction on circles of radii r from the hypothesis to show coefficients a_n vanish for n > s by letting r→∞ along the sequence; this is the final ingredient in deducing the exponential factor in Hadamard is e^{P(z)} with P polynomial degree ≤ k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gamma function integral definition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integral converges for positive s due to integrability near 0 (t^{s−1}) and exponential decay at infinity. Used as starting definition before analytic continuation; proofs often work on strips and use uniform convergence arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence relation for Gamma (Lemma 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Re(s) > 0, Γ(s+1) = s Γ(s). Consequently Γ(n+1) = n! for n = 0,1,2,...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtained by integration by parts on the integral definition and used to meromorphically continue Γ and to compute residues and special values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meromorphic continuation and poles of Gamma (Theorem 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Γ(s) extends to a meromorphic function on C with only simple poles at s = 0, −1, −2, ...; residue at s = −n is (−1)^n/n!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation obtained by repeated use of the recurrence Γ(s+1)=sΓ(s) and defining F_m(s)=Γ(s+m)/((s+m−1)⋯s) in half-planes Re(s) > −m. Alternative proof via splitting the integral at 1 and expanding e^{−t} yields a meromorphic series representation showing the poles and residues explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection (functional) formula for Gamma (Theorem 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For all s ∈ C, Γ(s) Γ(1−s) = π / sin(π s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved for 0<s<1 by integral manipulations (double integral after change of variables) together with a standard integral identity ∫_0^∞ v^{a−1}/(1+v) dv = π/ sin πa; then extended to all s by analytic continuation. Yields special value Γ(1/2)=√π.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties and growth of 1/Γ (Theorem 1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) 1/Γ(s) is entire with simple zeros at s = 0, −1, −2, ... and nowhere else. (ii) Growth bound: |1/Γ(s)| ≤ c_1 e^{c_2 |s| log|s|}, so 1/Γ is of order 1 (for every ε>0 one has bound ≤ c(ε) e^{c_2 |s|^{1+ε}}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses reflection formula to cancel poles of Γ(1−s) against zeros of sin πs, and series/integral representations plus crude factorial bounds to obtain the growth estimate. Concludes 1/Γ fits hypotheses for Hadamard factorization of order 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass product for 1/Γ (Theorem 1.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1/Γ(s) = e^{γ s} s Π_{n=1}^∞ (1 + s/n) e^{−s/n}, where γ is Euler's constant γ = lim_{N→∞} (Σ_{n=1}^N 1/n − log N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by Hadamard factorization applied to 1/Γ (entire of order 1 with simple zeros at nonpositive integers). Determination of constant exponent uses limit relations and evaluation at s=1; Euler's constant appears as normalization. The presentation includes the justification of existence of the limit defining γ.
